title: Status migrainosus / refractory migraine (inpatient)
presentation: Migraine attack typical of the patient's prior attacks except for duration and severity: unremitting >72 h (remissions up to 12 h from medication or sleep allowed) and debilitating (ICHD-3 1.4.1)
Milder attacks that aren't debilitating are coded probable migraine (ICHD-3 1.5.1)
definitions: ICHD-3 1.4.1: patient with migraine with or without aura; attack typical except duration/severity; unremitting >72 h and debilitating; not better accounted for by another ICHD-3 diagnosis
If medication overuse meets ICHD-3 8.2 criteria, code medication-overuse headache plus the migraine type, not status migrainosus (ICHD-3 comment)

Evidence base: AHS grades come from ED trials of single migraine attacks (AHS 2025; AHS 2016); the DHE regimen comes from an uncontrolled inpatient audit of refractory chronic migraine, cluster headache and NDPH (Nagy 2011). Status migrainosus itself wasn't studied as a separate population

immediateActions.action: Confirm the attack matches the patient's usual migraine; if not, work up a secondary cause. Stop overused acute medications and any triptan
IV prochlorperazine 10–12.5 mg (low EPS risk) or bilateral greater occipital nerve block (AHS 2025 Level A); metoclopramide, ketorolac or SC sumatriptan are Level B options
Single-dose dexamethasone to reduce recurrence (AHS 2016 Level B)
IV DHE course if no label contraindication — antiemetic before every dose; see dosing conflict on the DHE item
Avoid opioids (hydromorphone: AHS 2025 Level A must NOT offer)

notes: Baseline before DHE (Nagy)
DHE label: with CAD risk factors, consider an ECG right after the first dose

workup.test: CBC with differential, BMP (incl. BUN, creatinine, glucose), Ca, Mg, phosphate, PT/INR, PTT
notes: Nagy pre-DHE baseline
DHE label: contraindicated in severe hepatic or renal impairment
DHE label: avoid in pregnancy (may cause preterm labor)
Nagy pre-DHE baseline

treatment.doseText: 10–12.5 mg IV, ± diphenhydramine 25 mg IV (as given in trials)
notes: Akathisia, sedation; treat akathisia with diphenhydramine or benztropine (AHS 2025)

Akathisia prophylaxis — sources disagree: AHS 2025 says anticholinergic premedication may reduce EPS (no trial cited); a class 1 trial adding diphenhydramine 50 mg to metoclopramide found no difference in EPS (AHS 2016)
EPS risk factors: personal or family history of EPS, younger age, longer use; typical antipsychotics highest risk (AHS 2025)
evidenceNote: AHS 2025: Level A – must offer, in patients at low risk of extrapyramidal symptoms; highly likely effective

treatment.doseText: 0.5–3 mL of 0.5% bupivacaine or 1% lidocaine per side
notes: Volume: recommendation says 0.5–3 mL; Table 2 lists 0.75–3 mL (AHS 2025)
Bilateral in the class I trials; better response with experienced injectors (≥7 prior blocks) in one trial
Watch the total local anesthetic dose (systemic toxicity)
Requires no local-anesthetic or injection-site contraindication
evidenceNote: AHS 2025: Level A – must offer; highly likely effective

treatment.doseText: 10 mg IV when prochlorperazine isn't appropriate or available
notes: 2016 trials used 10–20 mg; the 2025 recommendation is 10 mg
Akathisia
Combination with dexketoprofen helped in trials (dexketoprofen not on this card)
evidenceNote: AHS 2025: Level B – should offer; likely effective

treatment.doseText: 30–60 mg IV if no NSAID contraindication
evidenceNote: AHS 2025: Level B – should offer; likely effective

treatment.doseText: 3–6 mg SC; best early or while pain is mild
notes: Not with serious cardiovascular disease (AHS 2025)
Not within 24 h of DHE, ergotamine or another triptan (AHS 2016; DHE label)
evidenceNote: AHS 2025: Level B – should offer; highly likely effective; not Level A because inferior to prochlorperazine

treatment.doseText: 0.25 mL 1% lidocaine, if occipital blocks are insufficient or not an option
notes: Best combined with occipital block; occipital alone outperformed supraorbital alone (class I)
evidenceNote: AHS 2025: Level B — wording inconsistent: recommendation 'may offer'; narrative 'should offer'; Table 2 'Level B – May offer'

treatment.doseText: 400–1000 mg IV (≥800 mg may perform better)
notes: Likely inferior to dopamine antagonists and ketorolac (AHS 2025)
Label contraindications and interactions: see antiseizure-medications:valproate
evidenceNote: AHS 2025: Level C – may offer; possibly effective

treatment.doseText: 12.5–25 mg IV when prochlorperazine or metoclopramide aren't options
notes: Postural hypotension, sedation, akathisia — more adverse effects than prochlorperazine
evidenceNote: AHS 2025: Level C – may offer; likely effective, downgraded for adverse effects

treatment.doseText: 5 mg IV when prochlorperazine or metoclopramide aren't options
notes: Typical antipsychotics carry the highest EPS risk (AHS 2025)
evidenceNote: AHS 2025: Level C – may offer (2016 grade unchanged)

treatment.doseText: 2.75–8.25 mg IM when prochlorperazine or metoclopramide aren't options
notes: Akathisia and drowsiness in up to ~50%; rare life-threatening arrhythmias (AHS 2016)
evidenceNote: AHS 2025: Level C – may offer (2016 grade unchanged)

treatment.doseText: Recurrence prevention: single 10–24 mg IV dose (ideal dose unknown). Acute pain: 8–16 mg IV
notes: Meta-analysis of 3 placebo-controlled class 1 trials: NNT 9 for recurrence (AHS 2016)
Consider cumulative steroid exposure and glycemic control (AHS 2025; AHS 2016)
evidenceNote: AHS 2016: Level B – should offer to prevent recurrence; not re-assessed in 2025
AHS 2025: Level C – may offer for acute pain

treatment.doseText: 1–2 g IV; may be considered in migraine with aura
evidenceNote: AHS 2025: Level U – no recommendation; may be considered with aura

treatment.doseText: Nagy 5-day protocol: ondansetron 4 mg IV 30 min before each dose; 0.5 mg in 100 mL NS over 1 h → if tolerated, 0.75 mg in 250 mL over 1 h 8 h later → 1 mg in 250 mL over 1 h q8h × 10 doses (target cumulative 11.25 ± 1 mg). CONFLICT: exceeds the label maximum (IV 2 mg/24 h, 6 mg/week; not for chronic daily use)

dose.label: Nagy dose 2 (8 h later, if tolerated)

notes: Control nausea — it predicted failure to become pain-free (Nagy). Ondansetron 8 mg if nauseated at baseline; rescue: ondansetron 8 mg q8h or extra 4 mg PRN, promethazine 12.5–25 mg IV q12h PRN, slow infusion to 2–3 h, hold escalation or reduce dose
Domperidone (Nagy's other antiemetic) has limited US availability (Nagy)
Vitals (HR, BP, RR, temp, SpO2) before each dose (Nagy)
Leg cramps or joint pain: naproxen 500 mg q12h PRN (Nagy)
Transient headache worsening often settles with the next infusion; slow the next infusion (Nagy)
Higher cumulative dose predicted pain freedom; improvement continued up to a month after discharge (Nagy audit)
Stop immediately for signs of vasoconstriction — numbness, tingling, cold or pale digits, limb or chest pain (label)
Label: pleural/retroperitoneal fibrosis with prolonged daily use; don't use for chronic daily administration
Contraindications: next item
evidenceNote: Nagy 2011: uncontrolled audit (n=163; 114 chronic migraine)
AHS 2025 / 2016: DHE IV/SC Level U – no recommendation (ED trials didn't test the repetitive inpatient protocol)
DHE PI (Provepharm, rev 2/2025): Dosage and Administration, Warnings

treatment.doseText: Don't give with: potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (boxed warning — ritonavir, nelfinavir, indinavir, erythromycin, clarithromycin, troleandomycin, ketoconazole, itraconazole); ischemic heart disease or coronary vasospasm; uncontrolled hypertension; triptan, ergot or methysergide within 24 h; hemiplegic or basilar migraine; peripheral arterial disease; sepsis; after vascular surgery; severe hepatic or renal impairment; ergot hypersensitivity; peripheral or central vasoconstrictors. Avoid in pregnancy
notes: CAD risk factors (HTN, hyperlipidemia, smoking, obesity, diabetes, family history, postmenopausal women, men >40): label strongly advises against unless a cardiovascular evaluation is satisfactory
Less potent CYP3A4 inhibitors with caution: saquinavir, nefazodone, fluconazole, grapefruit juice, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, zileuton, clotrimazole
Breastfeeding: not during treatment or for 3 days after the last dose (label)
Nagy's protocol list adds any prior cerebrovascular event and any impaired liver or renal function
Use only with a clear migraine diagnosis — fatal cerebrovascular events have followed DHE given for symptoms wrongly attributed to migraine (label)
evidenceNote: DHE PI: Boxed warning, Contraindications, Warnings, Nursing Mothers
Nagy 2011 protocol appendix

treatment.doseText: Hydromorphone 1 mg IV: must not offer. Morphine 0.1 mg/kg IV: may not offer
notes: Inferior to prochlorperazine; more ED returns; risk of medication-overuse headache
Rare exceptions: no alternative, stable prior opioid response, low dependence/MOH risk (AHS 2025)
evidenceNote: AHS 2025: hydromorphone Level A – Must NOT offer (box and table; narrative says 'should NOT')
AHS 2025: morphine Level C – may NOT offer (2016 grade unchanged)

notes: Negative class 1 placebo-controlled trial
evidenceNote: AHS 2025: Level C – may NOT offer; likely ineffective

treatment.doseText: 50 mg IV as an analgesic — may not offer
notes: Still used adjunctively to treat akathisia (AHS 2025)
evidenceNote: AHS 2025: Level C – may NOT offer

pitfalls: AHS 2025 Level U (no recommendation): ketamine, IV lidocaine, propofol, IV caffeine, granisetron, IV ibuprofen, SPG block, eptinezumab, parenteral promethazine, trimethobenzamide; prolonged inpatient ketamine/lidocaine infusions weren't assessed
IV fluids alone didn't reduce pain (class II) — give them for dehydration from vomiting (AHS 2025)

Overused acute drugs (ergots, triptans, opioids ≥10 days/month) can cause medication-overuse headache (DHE label); Nagy stopped all overuse on admission and started preventives ~1 week after discharge
Not on card (US availability not addressed in sources): dexketoprofen, IV acetylsalicylic acid, IM diclofenac, lysine clonixinate; dipyrone is withdrawn from the US (AHS 2016)
escalateWhen: Attack differs from the patient's usual migraine, new focal deficit, or no response — reconsider a secondary cause (ICHD-3: not better accounted for by another diagnosis)
Chest pain or signs of vasoconstriction on DHE → stop DHE, ECG and evaluate before further doses (label)
institutionVaries: Who performs occipital/supraorbital nerve blocks on the ward
DHE order set, telemetry and infusion policy
